title: Carrot Cake
subtitle: Spiced carrot cake with cream cheese frosting
excerpt: A moist, warmly spiced cake made with grated carrot and oil, finished with a thick layer of cream cheese frosting. One of the most reliably good cakes to make from scratch.

recipe.sourceNotes: Carrot cake's history is often traced to medieval Europe, when carrots were used as a sweetener in cakes and puddings because sugar was expensive. The modern version using vegetable oil rather than butter and cream cheese frosting was popularised in the United States in the 1960s and 1970s, when it was marketed as a health food because of its vegetable content. By the 1980s it had become one of the most popular cakes in both Britain and America. Oil-based cakes stay moist for several days longer than butter cakes, which is one reason carrot cake is so popular for baking ahead. Walnuts and raisins are common additions.

recipeTools.notes: Two 20 cm round sandwich tins, greased and lined.

content.text: Grate the carrots on the coarse side of a box grater and squeeze out any excess moisture with your hands before adding. The frosting must be made with full-fat cream cheese: the low-fat version contains more water and produces a runny, unworkable frosting. Ensure the cream cheese and butter are both at room temperature before beating, or the frosting will be lumpy.
Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Grease and line two 20 cm sandwich tins. Whisk together the oil, sugar, and eggs in a large bowl for 2 minutes until well combined.

Fold in the flour, cinnamon, mixed spice, bicarbonate of soda, and salt. Fold in the grated carrot and walnuts (if using). Divide between the tins and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tins for 10 minutes, then turn out and cool completely.

Beat together the cream cheese and soft butter until smooth. Sift in the icing sugar and add the vanilla. Beat until light and creamy. Sandwich the cakes with half the frosting and spread the remainder over the top.
